Whether you need to locate a family member, friend, or conduct background research, this guide provides step-by-step instructions for conducting a Broward County Florida inmate lookup through verified government channels. How to Search Broward County Jail Records

  1. Visit the official Broward County Sheriff's Office inmate search portal. Navigate to the Broward County Sheriff's website and locate their inmate search tool. This database is updated regularly and provides real-time information about individuals currently housed in county facilities.
  2. Enter the inmate's basic information. You will need to provide the inmate's first and last name at minimum. If you have additional details such as a booking number, date of birth, or case number, these can help narrow your search results and ensure accuracy.
  3. Review the search results carefully. Once you submit your query, the system will display matching records. Results typically include the inmate's current location within the jail system, booking date, charges, bond information, and arraignment details. Multiple individuals may share similar names, so verify details before proceeding.
  4. Contact the Broward County Sheriff's Office directly if online results are unclear. Their inmate services team can provide additional information over the phone or help clarify search results. This is especially useful for recent arrests that may not yet appear in the online database.
  5. Check the Florida Department of Corrections if the inmate has been transferred. If the person is not listed in county records, they may have been transferred to a state facility. The Florida DOC maintains its own searchable inmate locator system for incarcerated individuals serving longer sentences.

Bail Bond Information for Broward County

When someone is arrested in Broward County, understanding the bail bond process is essential for families seeking quick release. Most bail bond companies operating in Broward County charge a standard fee of 10 percent of the total bail amount set by the judge. For example, if a judge sets bail at $10,000, a bondsman will typically charge $1,000 to post bail on the defendant's behalf. This fee is non-refundable, even if charges are later dismissed. Many bail bond companies in Broward County operate 24/7 and can expedite the release process, often securing release within hours of arrest.

The typical timeline for an arraignment in Broward County is within 24 hours of arrest for misdemeanor charges and within 72 hours for felony charges. During the arraignment, the judge reviews the case details and sets bail based on the severity of charges, the defendant's criminal history, employment status, and ties to the community. Some defendants may be released on their own recognizance (no bail required), while others may face bail amounts ranging from several hundred dollars to hundreds of thousands depending on the charges. Working with a reputable bail bond agency can help navigate this process and ensure compliance with all conditions of release.

Visitation Rules at Broward County Jail

  • Valid identification required: All visitors must present a government-issued photo ID such as a driver's license, passport, or state ID card. Children and minors must be accompanied by an adult with valid identification.
  • Visitation hours: Standard visitation hours are typically Tuesday through Sunday from 9:00 AM to 11:30 AM and 1:00 PM to 4:00 PM. Holiday schedules may vary, and it is recommended to confirm hours by contacting the facility directly before planning a visit.
  • Dress code requirements: Visitors must dress appropriately and professionally. Clothing should be clean and cover the shoulders, chest, and knees. Avoid bright colors, revealing clothing, and items that resemble inmate uniforms. Jewelry should be minimal and simple.
  • Video visitation options: Broward County offers video calling services for those unable to visit in person. These services are available through approved third-party platforms and may involve a fee. Contact the facility for specific information about available video visitation schedules.
  • Children's visitation policy: Children are permitted to visit but must be supervised at all times by an adult. The facility requests that children under 10 be kept to a minimum during visits, as they may find the environment disturbing. All children must comply with the same identification and dress code requirements as adults.

What to Expect After Arrest in Broward County

  1. Booking and intake process. Upon arrival at the Broward County Jail facility, the arrestee is booked into the system. This involves recording personal information, photographing, fingerprinting, and cataloging all personal belongings. The booking process typically takes 1 to 3 hours depending on facility volume and complexity of the charges.
  2. Medical evaluation and health screening. All newly arrested individuals undergo a medical and mental health screening to identify any immediate health concerns, medication needs, or psychiatric conditions. This step ensures the safety and wellbeing of both the inmate and facility staff.
  3. Classification and housing assignment. Based on the severity of charges, criminal history, behavior during booking, and other factors, the inmate is classified and assigned to an appropriate housing unit. High-security charges may result in solitary or restricted housing, while lower-level offenses may be placed in general population.
  4. Initial appearance and arraignment. Within the required timeframe, the inmate is brought before a judge for arraignment. During this hearing, charges are formally announced, bail is set, and the defendant is informed of their rights. This is also when bail bond arrangements can be finalized.
  5. Transfer or continued detention. Following arraignment, the inmate may be released on bail, transferred to a state facility if sentenced, or remain in county custody while awaiting trial. Transfers to state prison typically occur after sentencing to a facility that matches the length and security level of the sentence.

How to Contact Broward County Jail

Direct communication with the Broward County Sheriff's Office is often the fastest way to get accurate information about an inmate's status, charges, bail information, and visitation details. The department maintains phone lines dedicated to inmate inquiries and can provide assistance with locating records, clarifying search results, and answering questions about facility procedures. Staff members are generally available during standard business hours, and emergency calls are handled 24/7.

Frequently Asked Questions — Broward County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Broward County jail?

The most reliable way is to use the official Broward County Sheriff's inmate search tool on their website. You can search by the person's first and last name, and results will include their booking information, current location within the facility, charges, and bail status. If the online search does not return results, contact the Sheriff's Office directly by phone to speak with an inmate services representative who can manually search the database.

How long does booking take in Broward County?

The booking process at Broward County Jail typically takes 1 to 3 hours from the time of arrival. This duration depends on facility staffing, the complexity of charges, whether the person has outstanding warrants, and overall jail volume. During peak times or weekends, booking may take longer. Once booking is complete, the inmate's information will appear in the online search system.

Can I visit an inmate at Broward County jail?

Yes, visitation is permitted during scheduled hours, which are generally Tuesday through Sunday from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM with breaks midday. All visitors must present a valid government-issued photo ID and follow dress code requirements. It is recommended to call ahead to confirm hours and any special visitation restrictions that may apply to the inmate's classification or pending charges.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

If your search does not find the inmate in Broward County records, they may have been transferred to a state prison facility, released, or arrested in a different county. Check the Florida Department of Corrections inmate locator for state facilities, or contact the Sheriff's Office to ask if the person was transferred. If the arrest was recent and local, the information may simply not yet be in the online system.
